biggest_catch: The annual fee is $0 for the first 12 months and $99 after, so first-year math is clean: 50,000 AAdvantage miles after $2,500 in 3 months minus $0 = the full miles bonus; budget for the $99 fee hitting in year two if you keep the card.
catches: Claim the bonus only with spending you already planned; never buy things you don't need just to hit the $2,500 target.
The annual fee is $0 the first year and $99 from year two — it does not touch the first-year bonus, but factor it into whether you keep the card.
Applying for the card causes a hard credit inquiry, which can temporarily lower your credit score.
The variable purchase APR is 19.49%–29.49%; carrying a balance wipes out the bonus value — pay the statement balance in full every month.

Bonus miles are not available if you received a new account bonus for a Citi/AAdvantage Platinum Select account in the past 48 months, or converted another Citi card on which you earned a bonus in the last 48 months into one (Citi's 48-month same-product rule).
Miles typically appear in your AAdvantage account 8–10 weeks after you meet the spend — keep the account open until they land.

steps: Go to the official Citi page https://www.citi.com/credit-cards/travel-reward-credit-cards?afc=106 and read the Platinum Select bonus terms (50,000 miles after $2,500 in 3 months; $0 intro fee, $99 after).
Confirm you have not received a Platinum Select new-account bonus in the past 48 months (and have not converted a bonus-earning Citi card into one in the last 48 months).
Apply online through the official Citi page and get approved; save your approval confirmation.
Within the first 3 months of account opening, put $2,500 of already-planned purchases on the card — never extra spending for the bonus.
Pay the statement balance in full every month — the variable APR is 19.49%–29.49%; carrying a balance destroys the bonus math.
Keep the account open and check your American Airlines AAdvantage account — the 50,000 miles typically appear 8–10 weeks after you meet the spend.
Before month 12, decide whether the $99 year-two fee is worth keeping the card (free checked bag, preferred boarding) or downgrade/cancel.
